title: Non-User Privacy Notice | Hark
text:

Non-User Privacy Notice

Hark trains and operates third-party and proprietary large language models (the “Models” and each a “Model”) that may process personal data obtained from third-party sources during training and service delivery. This Non-User Privacy Notice (“Notice”) is intended to inform individuals who are not users of Hark's services ("Non-Users") regarding Hark’s collection, use, and processing of personal data to train and develop the Models (“Training Data”).

If you are a Non-User and have a question about your rights regarding our Training Data, please see Section 5 below for further information. Our contact details, along with information on the relevant controller of your information, are set out in Section 11 below.

1. Nature of Services
Hark is a content-based generative AI system designed to assist users with many tasks. To provide our services, we need to train the Models based on a variety of data.
2. Model Training Methodology
Pre-Training or Mid-Training. For proprietary Models, pre-training and/or mid-training involves the analysis of content to enable the Model to understand language fundamentals, including syntax, patterns, and connections between words, as well as foundational facts. Content is converted into "tokens" (discrete text segments), and the Model processes this content to build a complex network of relationships between tokens.
Fine Tuning. Hark also fine-tunes third-party Models. AI model fine-tuning is the process of taking a pre-trained, general-purpose model and further training it on a smaller, specialized dataset to make it proficient at a specific task or domain. It is a form of transfer learning where the Model, which already understands basic patterns, adapts its existing knowledge to new, niche requirements.
Post-Training. Post-training incorporates human feedback to improve Model usefulness, effectiveness, and safety. The Model generates multiple responses to prompts, which are evaluated by human reviewers based on quality, helpfulness, safety, and accuracy criteria.
Technical Clarification. Models do not store text in database form nor produce outputs by combining or collaging existing content. Models identify general patterns in text and do not retain access to original training data following completion of training.
3. Collection of Training Data
Sources of Training Data. Hark may obtain Training Data from the following third-party sources:
Data from Public Sources: Publicly available information via the Internet, including public records, social media platforms and other publicly available; and
Licensed Data Sets: Datasets obtained through agreements with third-party businesses.
Incidental Collection. Hark does not actively seek to collect personal data for Model training purposes. However, given the prevalence of personal information on the Internet, Training Data may incidentally include personal data.
Limitation on Use. Personal data included in Training Data is used solely to enable Models to learn about language and to understand and respond to user inputs. Such personal data shall not be used to: (a) contact individuals; (b) build profiles; (c) market products or services; or (d) sell information to third parties.
4. Privacy Safeguards
Data Collection Safeguards. We deploy restrictions for data obtained from the web, namely:
we do not access password-protected pages;
we do not bypass CAPTCHA controls; and
we respect "Do Not Crawl" signals (robots.txt).
5. How Non-Users Can Exercise Their Data Subject Rights
General Provisions. Non-Users located in certain jurisdictions, including the European Economic Area, Switzerland or the UK (the “European Region” ) have certain data protection rights. These rights are not absolute. In addition, when we do receive personal data from third parties as part of our Training Data, the information is not stored in a way that allows Hark to reasonably identify which information belongs to a particular person. As a result, we don’t provide the ability to access, download, correct or delete personal data received from third parties that may be used to develop and improve Hark’s Models and Services.
Complaints. If you are located in the European Region, you have the right to lodge a complaint about our data protection practices with the supervisory authority of your country or state. In Ireland, the relevant data protection authority is the Data Protection Commission, 6 Pembroke Row Dublin 2. D02 X963 Ireland, +353 017650100 / + 353 1800437737, email: info@dataprotection.ie or by using this online form. In the UK, the relevant data protection authority is the Information Commissioner's Office, Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire, SK9 5AF, +44 (0303) 123 1113, email: casework@ico.org.uk. In Switzerland, the relevant data protection authority is the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, Feldeggweg 1, CH - 3003 Berne, Switzerland, +41 (0)58 462 43 95, online contact form.
6. Legal Bases for Processing

In certain jurisdictions, like the European Region, Hark is required to have a legal basis for processing personal data. Where relevant and applicable, we rely on our legitimate interests and the legitimate interests of others to process any personal data that may form part of our Training Data. It is in our interests, the interests of our users and the public interest, to build and sustain AI tools that enable people and businesses to communicate freely, discover meaningful information, and engage with content that matters to them. Achieving these legitimate interests is not possible without the use of large datasets, which may include personal data.

7. Disclosure of Training Data
Hark may disclose TrainingData to the following categories of recipients:
Affiliates. Entities that control, are controlled by, or are under common control with Hark, provided such affiliates use Training Data consistent with this Notice; and
Service Providers and Business Partners. Third parties engaged for data analysis, research, cloud storage and other purposes related to the development and improvement of the Models, , who shall access, process, or store Training Data only in accordance with Hark's instructions.
8. International Data Transfers
Training Data may be transferred to our servers in other countries, including the United States or countries outside of the European Region .
Where information is transferred outside of the European Region, we ensure it benefits from an adequate level of data protection by relying on: For transfers outside of the European Region, Hark relies upon:
Adequacy Decisions. Determinations by the European Commission under Article 45 GDPR (or equivalent) recognizing adequate levels of data protection; or
Standard Contractual Clauses. Contractual clauses approved by the European Commission under Article 46 GDPR, or approved equivalents for the UK and Switzerland, that allow companies to transfer data outside the EEA. These (and their approved equivalent for the UK and Switzerland) are called standard contractual clauses. Where we rely on standard contractual clauses, you have a right to request a copy of these by contacting us at privacy@hark.com
In certain situations, we rely on derogations provided for under applicable data protection law to transfer information to a third country.
9. Data Retention
Hark retains Training Data for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes outlined in this Notice.
Upon expiration of the retention period, Training Data shall be destroyed, deleted, erased, or anonymized in accordance with applicable law.
10. Controller and Contact Information
Controller. The organisation responsible for your personal data is Hark Labs, Inc.
Contact Information. If you have any questions about this Notice, or have any questions, complaints or requests regarding your personal data, you can contact us as described below:

By mail: Hark Labs, Inc. , 4000 N First St, San Jose, CA 95134.

By email: privacy@hark.com
